title: Shumard — Permian fossils from the Guadalupes
summary: G. G. Shumard visited the Texas Guadalupes with Capt. John Pope's survey; fossils he collected were identified by B. F. Shumard as resembling Permian faunas of Europe — among the earliest geologic observations of the range.
citations: Shumard, B.F., 1858, Notice of fossils from the Permian strata of Texas and New Mexico obtained by the United States expedition under Capt. John Pope…: Transactions of the Academy of Science of St. Louis, v. 1 (volume date often given as 1860). Context summarized in Hayes (1964, USGS PP 446, Introduction).

title: Richardson names Delaware Mountain and Capitan formations
summary: G. B. Richardson's Trans-Pecos reconnaissance names the Delaware Mountain Formation (sandstone and limestone of the Delaware and Guadalupe Mountains) and Capitan Limestone — the parent nomenclature later split into the Delaware Mountain Group.
orgs: University of Texas Mineral Survey
citations: Richardson, G.B., 1904, Report of a reconnaissance in Trans-Pecos Texas north of the Texas and Pacific Railway: University of Texas Mineral Survey Bulletin 9, 119 p. (Geolex original reference for Delaware Mountain).

title: Girty — USGS Professional Paper 58 The Guadalupian Fauna
summary: George H. Girty's USGS Professional Paper 58 monographs fossils from Capitan and Delaware Mountain strata of the southern Guadalupe Mountains — the classic paleontologic baseline for Guadalupian faunas.
orgs: USGS
citations: Girty, G.H., 1908, The Guadalupian Fauna: USGS Professional Paper 58, 651 p., https://doi.org/10.3133/pp58

title: Beede geologic map of part of West Texas
summary: BEG syntheses credit Beede (1924) with recognizing a lithologic tripartite character in Delaware Mountain sandstone that later underpinned King's three-formation subdivision. Primary item is University of Texas Bulletin 2607.
orgs: University of Texas
citations: Beede, J.W., 1924, Geologic map of a part of West Texas: University of Texas Bulletin 2607. Tripartite role as summarized by BEG DMG synthesis (Dutton et al.).

title: King — Brushy Cherry and Bell Canyon named
summary: P. B. King describes the Delaware Mountain Group and its Brushy Canyon, Cherry Canyon, and Bell Canyon Formations (names already credited to him in DeFord and Lloyd, 1940). Formal lithostratigraphic frame for the western escarpment and Delaware Basin fill.
orgs: USGS;AAPG
citations: King, P.B., 1942, Permian of west Texas and southeastern New Mexico: AAPG Bulletin, v. 26, no. 4, p. 535–763. See also DeFord, R.K., and Lloyd, E.R., 1940, AAPG Bulletin, v. 24, p. 1–14 (names credited to King).

title: King — USGS Professional Paper 215 southern Guadalupes
summary: USGS Professional Paper 215 maps and describes the southern Guadalupe and adjacent Delaware Mountains Permian section, including Brushy Canyon stratigraphy and relations along the western escarpment.
orgs: USGS
citations: King, P.B., 1948, Geology of the Southern Guadalupe Mountains, Texas: USGS Professional Paper 215, 183 p., https://doi.org/10.3133/pp215

title: Hayes — USGS Professional Paper 446 New Mexico Guadalupes
summary: USGS Professional Paper 446 maps Guadalupe Mountains geology in New Mexico and discusses Delaware Mountain Group / Capitan shelf–reef–basin relations north of King's Texas map area.
orgs: USGS
citations: Hayes, P.T., 1964, Geology of the Guadalupe Mountains, New Mexico: USGS Professional Paper 446, 69 p., https://doi.org/10.3133/pp446

title: Harms — Brushy Canyon deep-water density-current deposit
summary: J. C. Harms interprets the Brushy Canyon Formation as a deep-water density-current deposit (GSA Bulletin). Widely cited turning point in Brushy Canyon process models.
citations: Harms, J.C., 1974, Brushy Canyon Formation, Texas: A deep-water density current deposit: Geological Society of America Bulletin, v. 85, p. 1763–1784.

title: Harms and Williamson — DMG saline density currents
summary: Harms and Williamson argue Delaware Mountain Group siltstones and channelized sandstones (including Brushy and Bell Canyon) were deposited by saline density currents in a density-stratified basin, contrasting with turbidity-current submarine-fan models.
citations: Harms, J.C., and Williamson, C.R., 1988, Deep-water density current deposits of Delaware Mountain Group (Permian), Delaware Basin, Texas and New Mexico: AAPG Bulletin, v. 72, p. 299–317.

title: Rossen M.S. thesis — Brushy Canyon onlap area
summary: Christine Rossen M.S. thesis on Brushy Canyon sedimentology in the Guadalupe Mountains onlap area (University of Wisconsin–Madison). Cited as foundational outcrop work preceding later Exxon publications.
orgs: University of Wisconsin–Madison
citations: Rossen, C., 1985, Sedimentology of the Brushy Canyon Formation (Permian, Early Guadalupian) in the onlap area, Guadalupe Mountains, west Texas: M.S. thesis, University of Wisconsin–Madison, 314 p.

title: Rossen and Sarg — 1987 AAPG abstract
summary: AAPG abstract on Brushy Canyon–Cherry Canyon Tongue sedimentology and regional correlation. Abstract favors turbidity currents over hypersaline density currents based on onlap geometry, channels, and shelfward correlation.
citations: Rossen, C., and Sarg, J.F., 1987, Sedimentology and regional correlation of a basinally restricted deep-water siliciclastic wedge: Brushy Canyon Formation–Cherry Canyon Tongue (Lower Guadalupian), Delaware Basin: AAPG Bulletin, v. 71 (abstract).

title: Zelt and Rossen — Brushy Canyon in deep-water atlas
summary: Chapter documenting geometry and continuity of Brushy Canyon deep-water sandstones and siltstones along Guadalupe–Delaware Mountains outcrops.
citations: Zelt, F.B., and Rossen, C., 1995, Geometry and continuity of deep-water sandstones and siltstones, Brushy Canyon Formation (Permian) Delaware Mountains, Texas, in Pickering, K.T., and others, eds., Atlas of Deep Water Environments: Springer.
